newsitem.title: USA: Heavy snow slows Iowa, Dakotas livestock movement.
newsitem.headline: Heavy snow slows Iowa, Dakotas livestock movement.

text.p: Up to one foot of snow fell in parts of northwest Iowa and the Dakotas over the weekend, hampering livestock movement and prompting higher cash hog and cattle prices, meteorologists and livestock sources said.
"We had accumulations of mostly six to 12 inches in Sioux Falls (South Dakota) and northwest Iowa over the weekend," said Weather Services Corp meteorologist Joel Burgio.
Snow continued to fall in those areas Monday morning.
Livestock markets in Iowa and South Dakota were called to open $0.50 to $1.00 higher because of the winter weather, several livestock sources said.
"We've got a heck of a weather market out here," one South Dakota source said. "If it weren't for the snow I'd be going $0.50 lower."
Forecasts called for additional accumulation of two to four inches in the Dakotas and Iowa, moving east into central Iowa and Minnesota Monday afternoon.
